headline: Showers wind down Sunday and dense fog is likely by early Monday, followed by a warm Monday (highs in the 60s to near 70s), a cooler, more seasonable rest of the week, and increasingly likely widespread rain Wednesday into Thursday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Light showers continue on and off through much of Sunday across the area as east-southeast winds push moist air up over a layer of cool air trapped against the mountains; around Charlotte, light rain could linger until roughly 11 AM–2 PM, with low clouds and patchy reduced visibility. Gusty winds across the South Carolina Upstate this morning ease by late morning, and clouds may briefly lift this afternoon and early evening. By Sunday evening the cool-air layer breaks down as high pressure moves well offshore and the coastal low heads toward New England. With calm winds, clearing skies and lingering moisture, widespread patchy to dense fog is likely tonight into daybreak Monday, and the chance of dense fog has increased.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Monday will be noticeably warm ahead of a cold front, with highs in the low 60s to low 70s and a few spots in the southern Upstate nearing the mid 70s. The front crosses the area Monday night into Tuesday morning mostly dry, apart from a few mountain showers mainly along the Tennessee border. Tuesday turns cooler as a large high-pressure system settles over the Midwest and then moves toward the Mid-Atlantic and New England, setting up dry, cool northeast winds and another layer of cool air banked against the mountains, with dry weather lasting through Tuesday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A well-defined storm system is expected Wednesday into Thursday as a disturbance from the southern Plains helps a low form and strengthen along the Carolina coast, driving moist air inland, and confidence continues to increase that widespread rain will return across the area, with rain chances trending up. For now it looks like a beneficial rain with no hazards expected, but that could change as computer models come into better agreement. Temperatures stay cooler and more seasonable through the rest of the week.

watch_for: Dense fog late tonight into daybreak Monday.
How much rain the Wednesday–Thursday storm brings, and whether any hazards develop as forecasts come into better agreement.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in lingering showers today, fog early Monday, a warm Monday and a cooler, dry Tuesday, with growing but not complete confidence in widespread rain Wednesday into Thursday since models still differ on how the storm comes together.
